title: Start with the invitation, not a wall of instructions
why: The long how-it-works section pushed setup far down the page. A short overview now leads directly into step 1, with agent-tool requirements in a supporting disclosure.
before: The first screen is dominated by explanations; setup is below it.
after: Options and Create an invitation are visible much sooner.

title: Make copying a clear handoff
why: The prompt appeared below old instructions, Copy competed with Watch, and Copied disappeared after three seconds. The new heading receives focus, Copy prompt leads the section, the field has a visible label, and persistent confirmation explicitly asks the human to paste and send. The current invitation no longer duplicates itself in recent visits.
before: Prompt first, competing actions, and a transient Copied label.
after: One leading copy action; persistent paste-and-send guidance.

title: Explain what waiting means
why: The old connection message did not clearly distinguish a copied prompt from an agent opening it. A dedicated arrival section says what is being observed, asks the human to return to this tab, and explains automatic navigation. Troubleshooting and the optional visit-page link are secondary.
before: Watch competes with copying, followed by generic gate status.
after: Waiting is a separate step with a clear condition and next action.

title: Make blocked clipboard access recoverable
why: Copy errors appeared as a generic gate alert and left manual selection to the human. The new message is beside the prompt, the whole prompt receives focus and selection, and a successful copy retry clears the error. Copy failure does not discard or recreate the invitation.
before: Generic gate error and an unselected prompt.
after: Specific manual-copy instructions and the entire prompt selected.
